body.statement: At \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and \(\lambda=1000\), \(129113957/50000000\le L^\star_{4,2/5}(1000)\le64557127/25000000\), every global optimizer uses \(m=2\), and \([999.9,1000.1]\cap\mathcal B_{4,2/5}=\varnothing\). In particular, no balanced randomized response after a nontrivial binary partition is globally optimal throughout that interval. Separately, at \(N=4\), \(m=2\), \(\lambda=3\), and \(\alpha=1/10\), the mapping \(Q\mapsto-V_2(Q)\) is not convex, so the confidence objective is not representable by the convex-utility premise used for the generic extreme-point shortcut.
body.justification: The certified interval rules out a universal binary-optimality story and places the boundary search on a genuinely nontrivial equality set.
body.gap: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath and Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa prove binary or partition structure for single-draw divergence objectives, not this fourfold composite-confidence loss.
body.consumer: A protocol designer at these parameters must retain at least a nonbinary candidate family rather than restricting the acquisition layer to one-bit randomized response.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the exact four-unit certificate lemma at \((N,\alpha,\lambda)=(4,2/5,1000)\).  Its feasible four-output rule gives
\[
 \inf_QV_2(Q)\le \frac{64557127}{25000000}.
\]
Its simultaneous polynomial-dual certificate gives
\[
 \inf_QV_2(Q)\ge \frac{129113957}{50000000}.
\]
For \(m=1\), postprocessing dominance of the identity experiment and the exact identity-channel dual give
\[
 \inf_QV_1(Q)\ge\frac{637}{240}.
\]
The allocation-reflection lemma gives the same lower bound at \(m=3\).  Since
\[
 \frac{637}{240}>\frac{64557127}{25000000},
\]
neither \(m=1\) nor \(m=3\) can attain the global value, whereas \(m=2\) has a feasible rule at the smaller displayed value.  Therefore every global optimizer uses \(m=2\), and taking the minimum over allocations proves
\[
 \frac{129113957}{50000000}
 \le L^\star_{4,2/5}(1000)
 \le\frac{64557127}{25000000}.
\]

We next propagate the binary separation away from \(1000\).  For \(r\)-ary randomized response, one row has probability \(\lambda/(\lambda+r-1)\) at its high output and \(1/(\lambda+r-1)\) elsewhere.  Direct subtraction of two such rows at \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda_0\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{Q_{r,\lambda}(\cdot\mid x),Q_{r,\lambda_0}(\cdot\mid x)\}
 =\frac{(r-1)|\lambda-\lambda_0|}
 {(\lambda+r-1)(\lambda_0+r-1)}.
\]
For \(|\lambda-1000|\le1/10\), the sum of the product-experiment total-variation bounds for the binary and four-output channels is therefore at most
\[
 4\left(\frac{1\cdot(1/10)}{1000^2}
 +\frac{3\cdot(1/10)}{1000^2}\right)
 =\frac{16}{10\cdot1000^2}.
\]
Here the factor \(4\) is the number of units, and every denominator is at least \(1000^2\).  With \(2N+1=9\) and \(\alpha=2/5\), the value-modulus lemma bounds the sum of the two value changes by
\[
 9\left(1+\frac1{2/5}\right)\frac{16}{10\cdot1000^2}
 =\frac{63}{1250000}.
\]
At \(\lambda_0=1000\), the exact certificate lemma supplies one four-output feasible value \(U=25823/10000\) and, for every one of the seven complementary-pair representatives of nontrivial binary partitions, the common strict lower bound \(D=258239/100000\).  Their gap satisfies
\[
 D-U=\frac9{100000}>\frac{63}{1250000}.
\]
Thus throughout \([999.9,1000.1]\) the optimal confidence value of the four-output channel remains strictly smaller than that of every balanced binary-partition randomized-response channel.  Since the unrestricted optimum is no larger than the four-output value,
\[
 [999.9,1000.1]\cap\mathcal B_{4,2/5}=\varnothing.
\]

Finally take \(N=4,m=2,\lambda=3,\alpha=1/10\).  The exact certificate lemma defines a binary channel \(Q_b\), a four-output channel \(Q_f\), and their tagged midpoint \(Q_{\rm mix}=\tfrac12Q_b\oplus\tfrac12Q_f\), and proves
\[
 V_2(Q_b)>\frac{347}{50},\qquad
 V_2(Q_f)>\frac{737}{100},\qquad
 V_2(Q_{\rm mix})\le\frac{711}{100}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 V_2(Q_{\rm mix})<\frac{1431}{200}
 <\frac{V_2(Q_b)+V_2(Q_f)}2.
\]
Hence \(V_2\) is not concave on the common-channel class, equivalently \(Q\mapsto -V_2(Q)\) is not convex.  This proves every asserted clause.
